clue.text: A cry for mercy from Scrooge once before

parts.note: Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge was a miser before his Christmas change of heart
ere is the poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the reformed skinflint Scrooge begging for pity in his earlier days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' matters: Scrooge was a miser only before the ghosts reformed him in A Christmas Carol. The answer is the Latin psalm 'Have mercy', Psalm 51.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miserere is Psalm 51, whose opening Latin word is a plea to God for pity, so it is a prayer for mercy.

clue.text: I eventually hold party for devoted admirer

indicators.note: I and the word for eventually hold the party between them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: eventually means later, in time to come
do is a colloquial word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A fan resolves to throw a party for their hero sooner or later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like a verb about the party, but signals the container: the I and 'eventually' together wrap round the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships an idol, literally or figuratively, is a fervent worshipper or fan.

clue.text: I plan extreme fashion based on research

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means shape or make, so the letters of these three words are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone declares a radical new way of dressing, claiming it is grounded in scientific study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like the subject of the plan, but it is the verb signalling that I PLAN EXTREME is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Experimental work rests on tests and trials, so it is founded on empirical investigation.

clue.text: Future flier has a missile that is fragile

parts.note: an egg holds a bird that will one day fly
a shell is an artillery missile

explanation.surface: A bird yet to hatch is threatened by a projectile, which is a delicate situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the egg to the shell, and 'that is' leads to the definition. Eggshell describes something very thin and delicate, like eggshell china.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell as an adjective describes porcelain or other things thin and brittle, easily broken.

clue.text: Explosive device in tangled net is conspicuous

indicators.note: the explosive device goes in the jumbled net, so one piece sits inside the other
a tangled net has its strands, here letters, muddled up

parts.note: a mine is a buried explosive device

explanation.surface: A bomb caught in a knotted net stands out plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' turns NET into ENT, and 'in' signals the container. 'Explosive' suggests a blast, but it is just a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means prominent or standing out, notable to the eye or in reputation.

clue.text: Standing in for the real one playing the part

definitions.text: Standing in for the real one

explanation.surface: An understudy takes over the role from the star for a night.
explanation.definitionFit: An acting manager stands in temporarily for the permanent holder, and actors are performing a role on stage.

clue.text: Animated bear removes half of toy soldier

indicators.note: only one half of the toy's name is kept, the other half taken away

parts.note: a yo-yo is a spinning toy on a string
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A cartoon bear pulls apart a child's toy soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy soldier' looks like one thing, but the toy is a yo-yo, halved to YO, and the soldier is GI. Yogi Bear is the Hanna-Barbera cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is the picnic-basket-stealing cartoon character from Jellystone Park.

clue.text: Company head's resolution

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: The chief executive of a firm makes a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a boss but a headland, NESS in place names. 'Company head's resolution' reads like a boardroom decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution in the sense of determination or steadfastness of purpose is firmness.

clue.text: Maori can digest this food

indicators.note: digest means break down and rework, so these letters are broken down and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A New Zealander is perfectly able to eat this pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digest' pretends to be eating but signals rearranging MAORI CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tube-shaped pasta, an everyday dish.

clue.text: Exhaust works both ways

indicators.note: the word that means exhaust reads identically from left to right and right to left

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An exhaust system that functions in two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: Poop as a verb, chiefly British, means tire out: 'I'm pooped'. The clue's 'works both ways' says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To poop someone is to tire them out completely, an informal sense.

clue.text: Last one in seems converted to this doctrine

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are changed into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The final believer in seems to have been won over to a creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks religious but signals rearranging LAST, I (one), IN and SEEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentialism is the philosophical view that things have a fixed inner nature defining what they are.

clue.text: Not much determination, that is, shown by the emperor's son

parts.note: not much means little
will is determination or resolve
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone without much willpower, it seems, as displayed by a royal heir.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Willie was the British nickname for Crown Prince Wilhelm, son of Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany. 'shown by' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Willie was the First World War nickname for Crown Prince Wilhelm, heir of Kaiser Wilhelm II.

clue.text: Way to travel just a step

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for Street, a way or road
ride means travel, on a horse or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A walking enthusiast says moving one pace at a time is how to get about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'just' link the two pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single long pace in walking.

clue.text: A sign of refusal

parts.note: reads as a gesture like a shaken head, but also covers the minus sign and a reply of no

explanation.definitionFit: A negative is a reply of no, and the minus sign is called the negative sign.

clue.text: Tidy hospital worker

explanation.surface: A neat attendant on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means neat and well arranged, and an orderly is a hospital attendant doing non-medical jobs.

clue.text: Dismissed side completely

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
right is one side, as opposed to left

explanation.surface: A team was thrown out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Out is the cricket word for a batsman's dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly or entirely, as in won outright.

clue.text: Insinuates that one member is careless with the truth

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
lies means says untrue things, a pointed euphemism

explanation.surface: Someone hints darkly that a certain politician plays fast and loose with facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, which is what implying does.

clue.text: It's usually dark early in the day, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word spoken out loud is the one wanted, by sound not spelling

parts.note: the morning is the early part of the day

explanation.surface: A remark that it tends to be dark at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark' suggests night but refers to black funeral clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mourning dress, worn by the bereaved, is traditionally black.

clue.text: Made lord or earl in the finish

definitions.text: Made lord or earl in the finish

indicators.note: the peer goes in the word for finish, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the end is the finish
a lord or an earl is a member of the nobility, a noble

explanation.surface: Someone was finally elevated to the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: 'in' signals the container, and 'Made' only reads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ennobled is to be raised to the peerage, given a title such as baron or earl.

clue.text: Destroyed pirates' trail

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so the letters of the word are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: The path left by buccaneers has been wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trail' looks like a noun belonging to the pirates but is a verb: to trail around wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily or reluctantly, to trudge or trail about.

clue.text: One willing to examine eighteen letters

parts.note: test means examine
A to R covers the first eighteen letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone happy to inspect a large batch of mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' pretends to mean eager but means making a will. 'eighteen letters' is A TO R, the alphabet's first eighteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is someone who makes a will, so one who is willing in a pun sense.

clue.text: Bring down the equipment

explanation.surface: An order to floor the opponent and grab the gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle means bring down a player in rugby or football, and also means gear, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: International assembly meets with blow — relax

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is an assembly of nations
wind means a blow, a strong wind

explanation.surface: The United Nations faces a gale and needs to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meets with' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind is to let tension go, to rest and loosen up.

clue.text: In fact, Lionel's breaking voice undergoes this sort of change

definitions.text: voice undergoes this sort of change

indicators.note: breaking pretends to be a teenage voice breaking, but here the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Lionel's voice is breaking, which is a change in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' joins Lionel's voice in the surface but signals rearranging FACT LIONEL into FLECTIONAL, after the IN kept as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflection is the rise and fall of pitch in speech, so the voice changes in an inflectional way.

clue.text: Terrible skin

explanation.surface: An awful hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an old adjective means cruel or fierce (one fell swoop), and a fell is an animal's hide.

clue.text: Behold the French girl

parts.note: lo is an old word for behold, as in lo and behold
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: Look at the young French woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The French feminine article is LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lola is a female given name.

clue.text: Bags of assembly rooms to accommodate the aged

indicators.note: the rooms take in the elderly, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: halls are rooms for assemblies
old describes the aged

explanation.surface: Luggage from function rooms used to house the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accommodate' signals the container. A holdall is a large soft travel bag, chiefly a British term.
explanation.definitionFit: Holdalls are large soft travelling bags.

clue.text: Urge school bosses to produce intellectuals

parts.note: egg, as in egg on, means urge
heads are head teachers, the bosses of schools

explanation.surface: A call for headteachers to turn out clever pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text had a stray '!' after 'school'; the page prints none.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is an informal term for highbrow, studious people.
